newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX EUROYEN SLIP AS NIKKEI FIRMS, DOWNSIDE SOLID.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX EUROYEN SLIP AS NIKKEI FIRMS, DOWNSIDE SOLID.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures lost ground on Tuesday as Nikkei cash and futures markets clambered to a firm finish.
But dealers said the outlook for the Nikkei remained grim amid signs of continued economic weakness in Japan, which would in turn keep Euroyen and JGB futures well underpinned.
"There was just some short-covering on the Nikkei but on the whole, sentiment is still bad. So we're looking for a firmer Euroyen market," a dealer at a European futures house said.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended up 274.93 points to 19,099.11 in Tokyo while its September futures contract added 270 points to 19,120 on SIMEX.

Dealers said the Japanese interest rate market might be in for a period of consolidation after recent sharp gains but it would continue to take its cue from the Nikkei in the absence of fresh factors.

The lead March Euroyen contract stood at 99.21 at 1120 GMT after trading a thin 99.20-99.23 range against an IMM close at 99.24. Resistance is seen at 99.24/25 but a breach of that region could take the contract to 99.30.
September JGBs ended at 126.40 against a previous 126.62.
Eurodollar futures were scarcely moved before the release of U.S. retail sales and wholesale inflation data for July on Wednesday, dealers said.
"The longer term trend is down for Eurodollars but we're expecting weak retail sales numbers tomorrow. So there might be some short-covering," the dealer said.
He said there was growing speculation the U.S. Federal Reserve would hold rates steady at its policy-setting meeting on August 19.
December Eurodollars ended at 94.010 against their IMM close at 94.000 on light volume of 5,500 lots.
